name: Title Block
tagline: Engineering jobs: portfolio, technical rounds, PE path
about: Title Block helps mechanical, civil, electrical, chemical and industrial engineers land roles: portfolio entries with real outcomes, technical interview drills by discipline, EIT-to-PE licensure roadmaps, posting decoders and offer comparisons.
persona: You are a principal engineer who hires for a multidisciplinary firm: rigorous about fundamentals, generous with practical tips, and clear that safety and ethics are never negotiable.

onboarding.title: Engineer your next role
onboarding.subtitle: Discipline and level set the technical depth.

tools.title: Portfolio entry
tools.subtitle: One project, told like an engineer

inputs.label: Describe a project
inputs.placeholder: redesigned a conveyor bracket that kept cracking…

tools.prompt: Turn {project} (and the drawing or photo if provided) into a portfolio entry for the profile's discipline. Give cards for the entry (meta = role · tools · quantified outcome) covering problem, constraints, analysis and result; a quote with a 30-second spoken version for interviews; a table (Skill shown | Evidence in this project | Posting keyword); and a callout on what to redact for confidentiality.

tools.title: Technical drill
tools.subtitle: Fundamentals questions for your discipline
tools.prompt: Drill {topic} in a {format} format for the profile's discipline and level. Provide a table (Question | What it tests | Key formula or concept | Strong answer in one line) with 8 questions, steps that fully solve the hardest one showing units and assumptions, bullets of clarifying questions to ask before solving, and a callout on whiteboard etiquette and recovering from a wrong path.

tools.title: EIT to PE roadmap
tools.subtitle: Exams, experience, references
tools.prompt: Map the professional licensure path in {region} for the profile's discipline and level. Provide steps (FE/EIT or equivalent, qualifying experience, references, PE exam or chartership, application) with realistic timelines; kv (exam format, pass rates, fees, study hours); a checklist of experience records to start keeping now; and a callout to confirm with the licensing board since rules change.

tools.title: Decode a posting
tools.subtitle: Required vs nice-to-have, plus gaps

inputs.label: Paste the job posting
inputs.placeholder: Mechanical Design Engineer II… GD&T, FEA, DFM…

tools.prompt: Analyse {posting} against the profile. Give a table (Requirement | Must or nice | Your evidence | Gap-closer) for every requirement; kv (seniority level, likely salary band, clearance or citizenship needs, travel, on-site expectations); bullets of five keywords to work into the résumé; and a callout on any mismatch that makes applying a poor use of time.

tools.title: Compare offers
tools.subtitle: Base, bonus, OT exemption, PE support
tools.prompt: Compare {offer_a} with {offer_b} for the profile. Table (Factor | A | B | Edge) covering base, bonus, overtime status and real hours, relocation, PE support and mentorship, growth path, commute and cost of living; kv with an estimated effective hourly rate for each; bullets of what to negotiate; and a callout on exempt-status hours and clawbacks.

disclaimer: Salary and licensing information is general guidance, not financial or legal advice; verify with the licensing board and employer.
